claims.title: delete-old-rows: empty insertedIds causes `.not('id','in','()')` which is a Postgres syntax error
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**delete-old-rows: empty insertedIds causes `.not('id','in','()')` which is a Postgres syntax error**

When `toInsert.length > 0` but every row fails to return an `id` (e.g. `inserted` is `null` or an empty array due to a Supabase edge case), `insertedIds` stays empty. The delete then executes:
```
.not('id', 'in', '()')
```
This is invalid SQL in Postgres — an `IN ()` with an empty list is a syntax error, not a no-op. The original pre-PR code had a conditional branch (`if (insertedIds.length > 0)`) around the `.not(...)` clause precisely to guard against this. That guard was removed when the delete was moved inside the `if (toInsert.length > 0)` block, but `inserted` being null/empty is still possible even when `toInsert` is non-empty (e.g. a partial Supabase failure that returns `data: null` without setting `error`).

Fix: re-add the guard or throw early if `insertedIds` is empty after a non-empty insert.

The function is called at pipeline time where throughput is not critical.

claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**SOLD_BADGE_PATTERNS regex is anchored with `/i` flag but uses a character class that already covers case — minor, but the class-attribute pattern `class="[^"]*sold[^"]*"` will match `soldout`, `sold-badge`, and also arbitrary unrelated classes containing the substring 'sold' (e.g. `household`, `consolidated`)**

The pattern `/class="[^"]*sold[^"]*"|>\s*Sold\s*</i` will match any HTML attribute value or tag content containing the substring `sold` case-insensitively. This includes `household`, `consolidated`, `unsold`, `sold_count`, etc. A false positive here reclassifies an active listing as sold, corrupting the comp data. A more targeted pattern (e.g. requiring a word boundary or a known class name like `sold-badge` or `listing-sold`) would reduce false positives. As written, any page mentioning "household goods" or showing a sold-count would be misclassified.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
const SOLD_BADGE_PATTERNS: Record<string, RegExp> = {
  therealreal_active: /class="[^"]*\bsold\b[^"]*"|>\s*Sold\s*<\/[a-z]/i,
  poshmark_active: /"availability"\s*:\s*"sold_out"|>\s*Sold\s*<\/[a-z]/i,
}
```

claims.title: Broad catch in verifyComp silently swallows unexpected errors including OOM from large HTML bodies
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Broad catch in verifyComp silently swallows unexpected errors including OOM from large HTML bodies**

The `catch { return UNCONFIRMED }` block at the end of `verifyComp` will silently swallow any error thrown inside `readBoundedText` or the `identityConfirmed`/`soldPattern` checks — including `RangeError` from regex backtracking on a malformed page, `TypeError` from unexpected `res.body` shapes, or even a JavaScript heap OOM if `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` is ever raised. Since the function already returns `UNCONFIRMED` for every failure mode, a genuine programming error (e.g. a broken regex, a null dereference inside the loop) will be silently swallowed and look identical to a legitimate network timeout. At minimum, rethrow errors that are not `TypeError`/`DOMException` network errors so programming bugs surface in logs.

claims.title: readBoundedText leaks the reader lock when reader.cancel() throws
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**readBoundedText leaks the reader lock when reader.cancel() throws**

In `readBoundedText`, when `received > maxBytes`, `reader.cancel()` is called inside the `try` block but before the `finally`. If `reader.cancel()` itself throws (which is possible if the underlying stream is already in an error state), the `finally { reader.releaseLock() }` will not be reached because the thrown error propagates out of the `try` before `finally` executes — actually `finally` WILL execute in JS even if `reader.cancel()` throws, but `releaseLock()` will then be called on a stream whose cancel already threw, potentially throwing again. More concretely: `reader.cancel()` is async (returns a Promise) but is not `await`ed here, so the cancel fires and the function returns `null` immediately while the stream continues reading in the background. The reader lock is released (in `finally`) while the stream is still being consumed by the un-awaited cancel, which can cause a `TypeError: ReadableStreamDefaultReader.releaseLock: There are pending read requests` at runtime.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
        if (received > maxBytes) {
          await reader.cancel().catch(() => undefined)
          return null
        }
```

claims.title: SSRF risk: competitor comp URLs fetched without runtime hostname validation
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**SSRF risk: competitor comp URLs fetched without runtime hostname validation**

In `verifyComp`, the `isAllowedHostname` check runs against `comp.listing_url` before the fetch. However, `fetch()` in Node.js follows redirects by default (up to 20 hops). The post-redirect hostname check (`if (!isAllowedHostname(res.url, comp.source)) return UNCONFIRMED`) only triggers *after* the redirect chain completes, meaning any intermediate redirect to an internal address (e.g. `http://169.254.169.254/` for cloud metadata) will be followed before being rejected.

The fix is to pass `redirect: 'error'` or `redirect: 'manual'` to `fetch()` and resolve redirects manually, or to use a fetch implementation that supports blocking redirects to private IP ranges.

claims.text:

**delete-old-rows: empty insertedIds causes `.not('id','in','()')` which is a Postgres syntax error**

When `toInsert.length > 0` but every row fails to return an `id` (e.g. `inserted` is `null` or an empty array due to a Supabase edge case), `insertedIds` stays empty. The delete then executes:

claims.title: readBoundedText leaks the reader lock when reader.cancel() throws
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**readBoundedText leaks the reader lock when reader.cancel() throws**

In `readBoundedText`, when `received > maxBytes`, `reader.cancel()` is called inside the `try` block but before the `finally`. If `reader.cancel()` itself throws (which is possible if the underlying stream is already in an error state), the `finally { reader.releaseLock() }` will not be reached because the thrown error propagates out of the `try` before `finally` executes — actually `finally` WILL execute in JS even if `reader.cancel()` throws, but `releaseLock()` will then be called on a stream whose cancel already threw, potentially throwing again. More concretely: `reader.cancel()` is async (returns a Promise) but is not `await`ed here, so the cancel fires and the function returns `null` immediately while the stream continues reading in the background. The reader lock is released (in `finally`) while the stream is still being consumed by the un-awaited cancel, which can cause a `TypeError: ReadableStreamDefaultReader.releaseLock: There are pending read requests` at runtime.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
        if (received > maxBytes) {
          await reader.cancel().catch(() => undefined)
          return null
        }
```

claims.title: COOKIE_PAIRS_RE fails to match cookies with empty values
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**COOKIE_PAIRS_RE fails to match cookies with empty values**

The regex `^[^=;\s]+=[^;]*(;\s*[^=;\s]+=[^;]*)*;?\s*$` requires the first value segment to match `[^;]*`, which allows an empty value — that part is fine. However, the name portion `[^=;\s]+` disallows whitespace in the name. Real browser `Cookie` headers (especially when copy-pasted from DevTools) often have a space after the `;` separator (e.g. `a=1; b=2`). The inner group `(;\s*[^=;\s]+=[^;]*)` correctly handles that with `\s*` after `;`, so pairs beyond the first are fine. The real issue is that a leading whitespace in the pasted string will fail — the outer anchor `^[^=;\s]+` rejects leading spaces even if `trimmedValue` is already trimmed. This is a documentation/correctness mismatch: the comment says it accepts single pairs, but a paste that starts with any whitespace (unlikely given `trimmedValue`, but worth noting) fails. The regex is also anchored such that a valid trailing `;` with no following pair passes (the `?` makes the trailing semicolon optional). This is correct, but a paste ending in `; ` (semicolon-space) would fail. These are edge cases but they affect real DevTools pastes.

claims.title: Poshmark health-check validates `json.data` as Array but Poshmark's search API returns a paginated object, not a top-level array
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Poshmark health-check validates `json.data` as Array but Poshmark's search API returns a paginated object, not a top-level array**

The new check `Array.isArray(json.data)` will always return `'invalid'` for a valid Poshmark response. Poshmark's closet/search API returns an object like `{ data: { bundles: [...], ... } }` or similar, not a flat array. This means every valid Poshmark cookie will now be reported as `'invalid'` in the health badge, which is a regression from the previous `res.ok` check. Verify the actual shape of the Poshmark API response being hit here and adjust the guard accordingly.

claims.title: onSaved callback fires before the health-check response returns — badge may flash stale status briefly
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**onSaved callback fires before the health-check response returns — badge may flash stale status briefly**

`onSaved?.()` is called inside the `try` block immediately after a successful save. The parent's `onCredentialSaved` calls `refetchHealth({ fresh: true })`, which initiates a fetch but resolves asynchronously. Between `onSaved()` and the fetch resolving, the badge still shows the old status. This is a UX note rather than a bug, but if the save endpoint and health-check endpoint are close in latency, the badge may briefly show `valid` for an old (now overwritten) credential before showing the new status.

claims.title: `refetchHealth` is declared with `useCallback` but has no dependencies — the empty dep array is correct, but the `cancelled` flag will not protect against double-invocation
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**`refetchHealth` is declared with `useCallback` but has no dependencies — the empty dep array is correct, but the `cancelled` flag will not protect against double-invocation**

The `refetchHealth` function closes over `setHealth` (stable) and uses a local `cancelled` flag correctly. However, when `onCredentialSaved` calls `refetchHealth({ fresh: true })` while the initial mount fetch is still in-flight, both will race to call `setHealth`. The `cancelled` flag only guards the closure created by a specific call — two concurrent calls each have their own flag, and both will commit their result. This means the stale (cached) response from the first fetch can overwrite the fresh result if it resolves last. A ref-based abort controller would be safer here.

claims.title: verifyComp identity check uses `comp.title` words but `significantTitleWords` is called without the brand argument
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**verifyComp identity check uses `comp.title` words but `significantTitleWords` is called without the brand argument**

At the call site in `verifyComp`, `significantTitleWords(comp.title)` is called without passing `brand`. The new `brand` parameter in the suggested fix above makes this explicit, but even without that change: the filter `w !== brand.toLowerCase()` inside `significantTitleWords` is a no-op because the function signature has no `brand` parameter — the intent to exclude brand words from `otherTitleWords` is documented in the comment but not implemented. Multi-word brands (e.g. 'Louis Vuitton') will have their component words included in `otherTitleWords` and matched trivially.

claims.title: Poshmark JSON body check: `json.data` array check may reject valid auth on API shape change
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Poshmark JSON body check: `json.data` array check may reject valid auth on API shape change**

The new logic returns `'invalid'` when `json.data` is not an array. If Poshmark changes their search-results API shape (e.g., wraps it in a different key, adds pagination, or returns an object for empty results), every user with a valid cookie will see `'invalid'` in the badge. A 200 with any non-null JSON body is stronger evidence of valid auth than a shape check against an undocumented internal API; a shape failure should probably return `'unreachable'` (API changed) rather than `'invalid'` (bad credentials).

claims.title: refetchHealth closure captures stale `cancelled` flag across re-renders
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**refetchHealth closure captures stale `cancelled` flag across re-renders**

`refetchHealth` is defined with `useCallback` and depends on `[]` (no deps). Inside it, `let cancelled = false` and the cleanup `return () => { cancelled = true }` are correct for a `useEffect` cleanup — but `useCallback` does not return a cleanup function. When `onSaved` calls `refetchHealth({ fresh: true })`, the `cancelled` variable is scoped to that individual call's closure and is never set to `true` by anything, so if the component unmounts mid-fetch, the `setHealth` call will still fire on the unmounted component. The cleanup pattern only works when the function is called directly from a `useEffect` (which it is, via `useEffect(() => refetchHealth(), ...)`), but the manual `onCredentialSaved` call has no corresponding cleanup.

claims.title: significantTitleWords filters brand word by string equality after lowercasing — brand with spaces not handled
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**significantTitleWords filters brand word by string equality after lowercasing — brand with spaces not handled**

`significantTitleWords` filters out words equal to `brand.toLowerCase()`, but `brand` may be a multi-word string (e.g. `'Louis Vuitton'`). After splitting on non-alphanumeric characters, `'louis'` and `'vuitton'` will each appear as separate words. The filter `w !== brand.toLowerCase()` will not match either (`'louis' !== 'louis vuitton'`), so both brand words survive as 'other title words' and will always be found on the page, making `identityConfirmed` trivially true for any same-brand listing. The brand name should be split the same way and each component word excluded.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
function significantTitleWords(title: string, brand?: string): string[] {
  const brandWords = brand
    ? new Set(brand.toLowerCase().split(/[^a-z0-9]+/).filter((w) => w.length >= 2))
    : new Set<string>()
  return title
    .toLowerCase()
    .split(/[^a-z0-9]+/)
    .filter((w) => w.length >= 4 && !TITLE_WORD_STOPWORDS.has(w) && !brandWords.has(w))
}
```

claims.title: effectiveSoldComps reload from DB uses `r.source.endsWith('_active')` — TRR and eBay active sources may not match
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**effectiveSoldComps reload from DB uses `r.source.endsWith('_active')` — TRR and eBay active sources may not match**

In the `toInsert.length === 0` reload path, sold vs active classification relies on `r.source.endsWith('_active')`. If any source string stored in the DB does not follow the `_active` suffix convention (e.g. a source from a previous pipeline version, or TRR comps stored as `therealreal` rather than `therealreal_active`), those rows will be silently misclassified as sold comps, inflating confidence and producing a non-fallback price from asking-price data. Add a log line showing which rows fall into each bucket so misclassification is detectable.

claims.title: effectiveActiveComps reload uses `_active` suffix convention that is not enforced anywhere
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**effectiveActiveComps reload uses `_active` suffix convention that is not enforced anywhere**

The reload path distinguishes sold from active rows using `r.source.endsWith('_active')`. This convention is not defined in a shared constant or schema constraint, so a future source name change (e.g., `poshmark_active` renamed or a new source without the suffix) would silently misclassify rows — sold comps would be treated as active or vice versa, corrupting the fallback calculation. Define a shared constant or use a dedicated `is_active` column if the schema supports it.

claims.title: Reload-from-DB path computes confidence and price from stale, unfiltered rows
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Reload-from-DB path computes confidence and price from stale, unfiltered rows**

When `toInsert.length === 0`, the code reloads all existing `pricing_comps` rows and uses them as `effectiveSoldComps`/`effectiveActiveComps`. These rows were never passed through `deduplicateComps` or `removeOutlierComps` in this run — they may include duplicates and outliers from a prior run that had different filtering. This means a retry run that finds nothing new can produce a different (potentially worse) price than the original run, depending on what was previously stored.

claims.title: `onSaved` callback fires after a successful save, but `refetchHealth` called with `{fresh:true}` will race with the cache-write in the route
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**`onSaved` callback fires after a successful save, but `refetchHealth` called with `{fresh:true}` will race with the cache-write in the route**

When a credential is saved, `onSaved` calls `refetchHealth({ fresh: true })`, which hits the route with `?fresh=1`. The route bypasses the cache, runs live checks, writes the result to `healthCache`, and returns. This is correct. However, if the user saves multiple fields in quick succession (e.g., both eBay fields), each save fires an independent `?fresh=1` request. The last one to return sets the displayed health state, which may not reflect both updates if one request starts before the other's credential write has propagated. This is a minor race but worth noting since the fix (debounce or sequential refresh) is simple.

claims.title: `filteredActive` applies `deduplicateComps` then `removeOutlierComps`, but `deduplicateComps` may not work correctly on active rows if it deduplicates by listing_url
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**`filteredActive` applies `deduplicateComps` then `removeOutlierComps`, but `deduplicateComps` may not work correctly on active rows if it deduplicates by listing_url**

If `deduplicateComps` deduplicates by `listing_url`, active comps from TheRealReal (fetched via Google snippet) may have canonical URLs that differ from the actual listing URLs (e.g., tracking params, redirects). Two snippets for the same item with different URLs would both survive deduplication, inflating the active comp count and biasing the fallback median. This is a pre-existing risk, but applying `deduplicateComps` to active rows makes it newly load-bearing.

claims.title: significantTitleWords splits on non-alphanumeric but then filters w.length >= 4 — single-character splits produce empty tokens
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**significantTitleWords splits on non-alphanumeric but then filters w.length >= 4 — single-character splits produce empty tokens**

`.split(/[^a-z0-9]+/)` on a string like `'chanel bag'` (after `.toLowerCase()`) can produce leading/trailing empty strings if the input starts or ends with a non-alphanumeric character (e.g. `'Chanel® Bag'` → `['chanel', 'bag']` — fine here, but `'12" Chanel'` → `['12', 'chanel']`). The `w.length >= 4` filter catches most noise but empty tokens from leading/trailing separators pass `length >= 4` only if they are not empty, so this is only a latent issue. The real gap: two-character tokens like `'19'` (a bag style number) are dropped, which could cause identity to match a wrong-model listing of the same brand. Not blocking, but consider keeping short pure-numeric tokens that are likely style/size discriminators.

claims.title: filteredActive uses removeOutlierComps(deduplicateComps(relevantActive)) but relevantActive may be empty — deduplicateComps/removeOutlierComps must tolerate empty input
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**filteredActive uses removeOutlierComps(deduplicateComps(relevantActive)) but relevantActive may be empty — deduplicateComps/removeOutlierComps must tolerate empty input**

If `relevantActive` is empty, both calls receive `[]`. The correctness of this depends on `deduplicateComps` and `removeOutlierComps` not throwing on empty arrays. Since their implementations are not in the diff this is flagged as a low-severity question — if either uses `arr[0]` or `arr.length - 1` without a guard, `filteredActive` will throw and the whole step will fail.

claims.title: effectiveSoldComps fallback query has no `.limit()` — could return unbounded rows on a listing with many prior runs
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**effectiveSoldComps fallback query has no `.limit()` — could return unbounded rows on a listing with many prior runs**

The new reload query `supabase.from('pricing_comps').select('*').eq('listing_id', listingId)` has no row cap. A listing that has been retried many times (the replace-on-regen fix should bound this going forward, but old data exists) could return hundreds of rows, all of which then drive `calcConfidenceScore` and the median price. A `.limit(200)` or ordering by `created_at desc` with a limit would bound memory and prevent stale historical rows from dominating.

claims.title: toInsert.length === 0 reload path does not guard against DB errors — a failed select silently uses empty arrays
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**toInsert.length === 0 reload path does not guard against DB errors — a failed select silently uses empty arrays**

The reload query `await supabase.from('pricing_comps').select('*').eq('listing_id', listingId)` destructures only `{ data: existingRows }`, discarding the `error` field. If the select fails, `existingRows` is `null`, `existing` is `[]`, and `effectiveSoldComps`/`effectiveActiveComps` are both empty arrays — the fallback silently produces the same 'no data' result as if there were no existing comps, defeating the purpose of the drz fix.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
    const { data: existingRows, error: reloadError } = await supabase
      .from('pricing_comps')
      .select('*')
      .eq('listing_id', listingId)
    if (reloadError) {
      console.error('step3: failed to reload existing comps for drz fallback', reloadError)
    }
    const existing = (existingRows ?? []) as typeof compRows
```

claims.title: fresh=1 query parameter bypass added to GET handler but the cache key is userId — a ?fresh=1 request from any session invalidates the cache for that user across all sessions
claims.text:

**fresh=1 query parameter bypass added to GET handler but the cache key is userId — a ?fresh=1 request from any session invalidates the cache for that user across all sessions**

The cache is keyed by `user.id`. When `fresh=1` is set, the handler skips the cache read and will overwrite the cache entry with the new result. This is correct for single-session use, but if the user has two browser tabs open simultaneously and one sends `?fresh=1`, it triggers two concurrent live credential probes and the second write wins. This is a minor race but worth noting since the health-check fires live network requests.

**filteredActive applied to toInsert but effectiveActiveComps on zero-insert reload may include unfiltered rows from a prior run**

These rows were filtered at insert time by a prior run, so they are filtered — but a prior run using an older version of the code (before `filteredActive` was introduced) may have inserted unfiltered active comps. The reload does not re-apply `deduplicateComps`/`removeOutlierComps`, so the effective active comps on a zero-insert retry of an old listing may still be unfiltered. This is an edge case but worth noting.

**Comment says `filteredActive` uses both deduplication and outlier removal, but `deduplicateComps` is applied to `relevantActive` not `filteredActive`**

claims.title: New identity-check comment does not mention the case where `otherTitleWords` is empty for a multi-word title
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**New identity-check comment does not mention the case where `otherTitleWords` is empty for a multi-word title**

The comment explains the fallback: "If the title has no significant word beyond the brand (e.g. just 'Chanel'), fall back to the brand-only check rather than making identity unconfirmable altogether." But the condition `otherTitleWords.length === 0` triggers for any title whose non-brand words are all shorter than 4 characters or in the stopword list — not only single-word titles. For example, a title like `"Nike Air"` would have `otherTitleWords = []` after filtering `'air'` (3 chars) and `'nike'` as the brand, silently falling back to brand-only. The comment's example is too narrow and could mislead maintainers into thinking this only applies to single-word brand names.

claims.title: filteredActive dedupe/outlier removal applied after relevantActive is already used for fallback signal
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**filteredActive dedupe/outlier removal applied after relevantActive is already used for fallback signal**

The PR adds `filteredActive = removeOutlierComps(deduplicateComps(relevantActive))` but `relevantActive` is still referenced above this point for `lowestActive` computation (pre-existing). That is fine. However, the `effectiveActiveComps` reload path (`toInsert.length === 0`) fetches rows filtered only by `source.endsWith('_active')` and passes them directly to `calcConfidenceScore` and the median, without running `deduplicateComps`/`removeOutlierComps` on them. If a prior run wrote duplicate or outlier active rows (before this PR's filtering was in place), the reload path will compute a confidence and price from those unfiltered rows — inconsistent with what a fresh run would produce.

claims.title: effectiveSoldComps/effectiveActiveComps reloaded with `select('*')` — no dedup/outlier pass on reloaded rows
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**effectiveSoldComps/effectiveActiveComps reloaded with `select('*')` — no dedup/outlier pass on reloaded rows**

When `toInsert.length === 0`, existing DB rows are fetched and split into `effectiveSoldComps`/`effectiveActiveComps` without any call to `deduplicateComps` or `removeOutlierComps`. A prior run may have written rows that would now be filtered out, so the confidence score and suggested price derived from these rows can diverge from what a successful re-run would produce. Apply the same filtering pipeline to reloaded rows before using them for pricing computation.

claims.title: `verifyComp` enhanced with better logging and identity checking but `verifyAndReclassify` is still never called from this file
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**`verifyComp` enhanced with better logging and identity checking but `verifyAndReclassify` is still never called from this file**

The identity-confirmation improvement in `verifyComp` (multi-word title matching) is good, but `verifyAndReclassify` — the function that actually applies these results to update comp records — remains unconnected from `step3-pricing-research.ts`. The comment at line 187 explicitly acknowledges this. The implication is that all the new `url-verify.ts` logic, including the multi-word identity check, is exercised by zero production code paths in this PR. This is a dead-code correctness problem: TRR comps continue to be inserted without any sold/active reclassification regardless of what `verifyComp` returns.

claims.title: Cache bypass `?fresh=1` is user-controlled and bypasses the 60-second rate-limit on credential probes
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Cache bypass `?fresh=1` is user-controlled and bypasses the 60-second rate-limit on credential probes**

The `fresh` parameter is extracted from the request URL without any validation beyond string equality. Any authenticated user can call `/api/settings/platform/health-check?fresh=1` in a tight loop, bypassing the 60-second cache and triggering unlimited live eBay OAuth token mints and Poshmark network probes. The cache was the only rate-limiting mechanism. This was previously noted as a rate-limit concern; the `?fresh=1` bypass makes it worse by giving clients an explicit opt-out. At minimum, rate-limit the `fresh` path independently (e.g., per-user cooldown of a few seconds).

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Verified against the code: `reader.cancel()` is already `await`ed -- it isn't fire-and-forget. If it throws, the exception propagates through `finally { reader.releaseLock() }` (finally always runs in JS even when the try body throws) and up to verifyComp's outer catch, which returns UNCONFIRMED. No lock leak, no unhandled rejection. Not applying the suggested `.catch(() => undefined)` wrapper -- the existing error path already handles this correctly, and swallowing it earlier would remove information from the console.warn now added to the outer catch.
